title: Author removes any comment or reply at any depth: a 'comment removed' placeholder keeps visible replies in place, empty ones vanish, and public counts drop by one
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: C1 (derived from 'The author can delete any comment or reply, at any depth'): the pinned owner, and only the owner, can remove any comment or reply at any depth: missing
C2 (derived from 'from the report page'): the owner has a remove control on each comment drawn on the report page and on the branch page: missing
C3 (derived from 'or admin'): the owner can remove a comment from the admin side: missing
C4 (derived from 'it disappears for everyone'): once removed, the comment's text and author are shown to nobody (anonymous, reader, owner) on /reports/<slug>, the home page or a branch page: partial

C7 (derived from 'public comment counts drop by one'): a public visible-comment count exists wherever the report is listed or shown, and after a removal it is exactly one lower. A placeholder is not counted, and the visible replies under it still are: missing

Where the code lives: the remove handler in admin.go beside adminFeedbackReply (practice, chosen) or comment.go (crossdomain); SC-021's comments-side code in comments.go (practice) or a new internal/comments/block.go (crossdomain, chosen), with Remove kept in comments.go.
Lookup naming and shape: RemoveTarget returning (slug, published, err) (practice, chosen, mirroring OwnerReplyTarget) or Locate returning a Target struct (crossdomain).
The viewer flag through buildThread: a second bool parameter (practice) or a threadViewer{SignedIn, Owner} struct (crossdomain, chosen, so two adjacent bools cannot be swapped).
The landing field: `back` with a strict 400 on other values (practice) or `from` matched leniently (crossdomain). Chosen: the name `from`, with practice's strict parse.
Admin page: a 'N comments' line in the moderation section (practice) or none (crossdomain, chosen). Item element ids: mod-<n> (crossdomain) or none (chosen).
Where the Block form appears: inside the owner's details on reader pages and on the admin list (practice), or on the admin moderation list only (crossdomain, chosen).

A blocked account's refusal: per-package existing errors (404 for comments and feedback, a new ErrRefused 403 for votes; practice) or one ErrBlocked meaning 403 everywhere through a follow-up read (crossdomain, chosen).

Blocking an id that never signed in: refused 404 through INSERT…SELECT FROM users (practice) or allowed through INSERT…VALUES ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (crossdomain, chosen, per the migration's 'a block is a fact about an account').

All [SC-021] components: block.go (Block, Unblock, Blocked, ErrBlocked), the blocked refusal in Post, Cast, Withdraw and Send, the feedback 'blocked' mark and OwnerInboxBySender, the block, unblock and /admin/blocked routes with admin_blocked.html, and the Block forms. They belong to SC-021 (epic_parts). E-006 lines 1 and 2 cannot exit 0 until it lands.
Case 14, a removal racing 20 concurrent Posts. The design marked it material:false: Remove is one statement and the fitness rule already forbids the transaction that would cause BUSY.
Deferred findings m4 (landing at the parent's anchor), m5 (a remove form on the Blocked users page) and m7 (a shared or linked confirm page). They are decided deferrals.

No screens or app are declared. internal/config refuses to start without five HBAND_* variables, and the app command allows no environment, so the engine cannot open the app bare (#961). I rendered the owner's pages in Chrome myself instead.

SC-021 must build POST /admin/users/{u}/block and /unblock, GET /admin/blocked, the blocked refusal, and a remove form on each comment of the Blocked users page (m5, with a from=blocked landing). Until then E-006 lines 1 and 2 stop at a 404 on the block route.

Arrange a signed-in session for Chrome on this project (#961, #970): the owner's remove controls, summary disclosure and phone layout have only been rendered from harness-produced HTML, never as a signed-in browser session.

No planted finish body parses the owner's remove control; E-006 line 1 presses it by a hard-coded path. If E-006 should prove the control exists on the page, that is a change to that planted test, not to this slice.
Owner page weight at 10k comments (m7, #960): each shown comment now carries one more details/form for the owner.

deviation: modItem omits GitHubID and ParentID. The design lists both, but only SC-021's Block form would read them and nothing in this slice does, so they would be dead fields. SC-021 adds them with their reader.

deviation: TestFeedbackReplyMarkup (SL-009) pinned 'no number beside a comments label on the reader page'. That is untrue by design now that the reader page carries the count. I changed it to the observed new markup, exactly one count of 0, and did not loosen it.

deviation: TestStoreFaultSteps rows now take a world struct instead of (reader, top), and every subtest seeds a second comment and one feedback message. This is what the critic's fix to M1 requires: fresh targets for the removal rows and a message so the inbox's replies read runs.
deviation: The second fitness pattern is `removed_at = NULL` without the `|0` arm, per the critic's check (0 still means removed). The `because` names the holes.

deviation: Kept 'in reply to a removed comment' and ParentRemoved on the moderation list, as the design and case C-011 say. The m6 rename to ParentHidden was waived (O-019, note N-123), and until SC-021 a placeholder is always a removed comment.
